title: The Brothers Karamazov
author: Fyodor Dostoevsky

epigraph.text: Verily, verily, I say unto you, except a corn of wheat fall into the ground and die, it abideth alone: but if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit.

rights: Garnett’s 1912 translation is in the public domain. The Project Gutenberg source file keeps its license header. The annotations and commentary in this directory are CC BY 4.0.

pipeline.editorial:
- Show annotation IN PLACE: prefer inline (dotted-underline hover) notes wherever the note fits. Click-through only for deep material.
- `before`: only when the reader needs orientation for the passage to land (a real event behind a joke, a custom being performed).
- `after`: RESTRAINT. Only 2–4 per chapter, load-bearing analysis only. Never two blocks on one paragraph (merge instead). If the commentary already covers it, cut it.
- `page`: 2–4 per chapter — foreign passages (with `original` + `render`), real cases, institutions, plays/poems. Deep, structured material. The reader surfaces these ONLY as a solid underline + ❯ in the text — never duplicate them as blocks or cards elsewhere.
- `vocab` (type, placement inline): 8–12 per chapter. Words a strong non-native English reader half-knows: archaic/literary/period words, words whose older sense differs from the modern one, period objects. One-line dictionary definition in `note`, headword in `label`. NOT common words; when in doubt, leave it out.
- Annotations must never mix with the actual text — never put commentary-length material in inline notes.
- Target 25–35 annotations total per chapter.
- Commentary — exactly one voice, `scholarly`, 4 paragraphs. Scholarship is the spine, the scene is the evidence: organize each paragraph around a scholarly subject (an institution, the decade’s press, a source, a literary cult, a translation issue) and cite this chapter’s specific moments inside it. Strictly chapter-specific — nothing generic that could be pasted into any chapter. No plot summary, no generic praise of the novel.
